_about: Hand-written descriptions for nerves, brain, spinal cord and sense-organ structures without a Wikipedia text. See app/extra_content.py.

Ampulla of lacrimal canaliculus.description: Small dilatation of each lacrimal canaliculus at the bend where its short vertical part (about 2 mm, starting at the lacrimal punctum) turns medially into the horizontal part (about 8 mm) that runs to the lacrimal sac. A probe must follow this bend when the canaliculi are irrigated.

Vestibule.description:
The central, oval chamber of the bony labyrinth of the inner ear, between the cochlea in front and the semicircular canals behind. It contains the utricle and saccule, the otolith organs that sense linear acceleration and head tilt.
The oval window, closed by the footplate of the stapes, opens into its lateral wall; the vestibular aqueduct and the openings of the semicircular canals and cochlea also lead from it.

Zonular fibres.description:
The ciliary zonule (suspensory ligament of the lens): fine fibrillin-rich fibres that run from the ciliary body to the equator of the lens capsule.
In distant vision they are taut and flatten the lens; when the ciliary muscle contracts for near vision they slacken and the elastic lens rounds up (accommodation). Defective fibrillin in Marfan syndrome weakens them, causing upward and outward dislocation of the lens.

Aqueduct of midbrain.description:
The cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius): a narrow canal, about 1.5 cm long, running through the midbrain from the third to the fourth ventricle, between the tectum behind and the tegmentum in front. It is surrounded by the periaqueductal grey, a centre for pain modulation.
As the narrowest point of the ventricular system it is the commonest site of obstruction causing non-communicating hydrocephalus (aqueductal stenosis, or compression by a pineal or tectal tumour).

Base of peduncle.description:
The crus cerebri: the anterior part of each cerebral peduncle of the midbrain, a massive bundle of descending fibres continuous with the internal capsule. Its middle three-fifths carry corticospinal and corticobulbar fibres; the medial and lateral parts carry corticopontine fibres. The substantia nigra separates it from the tegmentum.
The oculomotor nerve emerges on its medial side, so a lesion here (Weber syndrome) causes an ipsilateral third-nerve palsy with contralateral hemiparesis.

Globus pallidus.description:
The medial, paler part of the lentiform nucleus, lying between the putamen and the internal capsule. Its external segment (GPe) belongs to the indirect pathway; its internal segment (GPi), with the substantia nigra pars reticulata, is the main inhibitory (GABAergic) output of the basal ganglia to the thalamus (VA/VL nuclei) via the ansa lenticularis and lenticular fasciculus.
The GPi is a target for deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease and dystonia; bilateral pallidal necrosis is typical of carbon monoxide poisoning.

Lentiform nucleus.description:
Lens-shaped mass of grey matter in the basal ganglia, made of the lateral putamen and the medial globus pallidus. It lies lateral to the internal capsule and medial to the external capsule, claustrum and insula; the putamen and caudate together form the striatum.
It is supplied mainly by the lenticulostriate branches of the middle cerebral artery, the classic site of hypertensive haemorrhage and lacunar infarction.

Mamillary body.description:
Paired round swellings on the underside of the posterior hypothalamus, behind the tuber cinereum, containing the mammillary nuclei. They receive the fornix from the hippocampus and project through the mammillothalamic tract to the anterior thalamic nucleus - part of the Papez circuit for memory.
They atrophy and may haemorrhage in Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome from thiamine deficiency, with profound anterograde amnesia.

Lingual gyrus.description: Gyrus on the medial surface of the occipital lobe, below the calcarine sulcus and above the collateral sulcus, continuous forward with the parahippocampal gyrus. The part bordering the calcarine sulcus is primary visual cortex representing the contralateral upper visual field, so a lesion causes a contralateral superior quadrantanopia; it also contributes to colour processing and word recognition. It is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery.

Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior do.description: The dorsal part of the posterior cingulate cortex, on the medial surface of the hemisphere above the corpus callosum, below the cingulate sulcus and the paracentral lobule. The posterior cingulate is a hub of the default-mode network involved in self-referential thought, memory retrieval and spatial orientation, and is among the first regions to show reduced metabolism in Alzheimer disease.

Paracentral sulcus.description: Short sulcus on the medial surface of the hemisphere that ascends from the cingulate sulcus and marks the anterior boundary of the paracentral lobule. The paracentral lobule, the medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri, contains the motor and sensory representation of the contralateral leg and foot and is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery.

Anterior occipital sulcus*.description: Variable, vertically running sulcus on the lateral surface of the posterior hemisphere, near the preoccipital notch. It is often taken as the boundary between the occipital lobe and the temporal and parietal lobes on the lateral surface.

Occipitotemporal sulcus (Lateral part*).description: Sulcus on the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes that separates the inferior temporal gyrus laterally from the fusiform (lateral occipitotemporal) gyrus medially. The fusiform gyrus contains the face-recognition and visual word-form areas.

Sulcus interm_prim-Jensen.description: The primary intermediate sulcus (of Jensen): a variable sulcus that descends from the intraparietal sulcus into the inferior parietal lobule, separating the supramarginal gyrus in front from the angular gyrus behind.

Transverse frontopolar gyrus and sulcus*.description: Small, transversely running gyri and sulci at the frontal pole, where the superior, middle and inferior frontal gyri end. The frontopolar cortex (Brodmann area 10) is involved in planning, multitasking and holding goals in mind.

Lat_Fis-ant-Horizont.description: Anterior horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus: a short branch running forward into the inferior frontal gyrus. With the anterior ascending ramus it divides the inferior frontal gyrus into the pars orbitalis (below), pars triangularis (between the rami) and pars opercularis (behind); the latter two form Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere.

Lat_Fis-ant-Vertical.description: Anterior ascending (vertical) ramus of the lateral sulcus: a short branch running up into the inferior frontal gyrus, separating the pars triangularis in front from the pars opercularis behind - both parts of Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere.

Lat_Fis-post.description: Posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus: the long main stem of the Sylvian fissure, running back and slightly upward between the frontal and parietal lobes above and the temporal lobe below, and ending by turning up into the supramarginal gyrus. The insula lies hidden in its depths, and the middle cerebral artery branches run within it.

Declive.description: Lobule VI of the cerebellar vermis, just behind the primary fissure, forming with the hemispheric lobule simplex (posterior quadrangular lobule) the first part of the posterior lobe. The vermis controls posture, axial muscles and gait; midline lesions cause truncal ataxia.

Folium of vermis.description: Lobule VIIA of the cerebellar vermis: a thin leaf of cortex between the declive and the tuber, at the back of the superior surface. It is continuous laterally with the superior semilunar lobule (crus I) and participates in the control of eye movements.

Pyramis of vermis.description: Lobule VIII of the inferior vermis, between the tuber in front and the uvula behind, separated from the uvula by the secondary (postpyramidal) fissure. It is continuous laterally with the biventral lobules.

Uvula of vermis.description: Lobule IX of the inferior vermis, between the pyramis and the nodulus, projecting down between the two cerebellar tonsils (which are its hemispheric continuation). With the nodulus it helps control eye movements and vestibular reflexes.

Tonsil of cerebellum.description:
Rounded lobule on the underside of each cerebellar hemisphere, beside the uvula and just above the foramen magnum, near the medulla.
Raised intracranial pressure can force the tonsils down through the foramen magnum (tonsillar herniation, coning), compressing the medullary respiratory and cardiovascular centres; tonsillar descent of more than 5 mm below the foramen defines a Chiari I malformation.

Anterior quadrangular lobule.description: Hemispheric lobules IV-V of the anterior lobe of the cerebellum, lateral to the culmen and in front of the primary fissure. The anterior lobe belongs mainly to the spinocerebellum; it receives the spinocerebellar tracts and contains a somatotopic map of the body, and degenerates characteristically in alcoholic cerebellar degeneration, causing gait ataxia.

Posterior quadrangular lobule.description: The lobulus simplex (hemispheric lobule VI): the first part of the posterior lobe of the cerebellar hemisphere, just behind the primary fissure and lateral to the declive.

Superior semilunar lobule.description: Crus I of the ansiform lobule (hemispheric lobule VIIA): a large part of the posterior lobe on the superior and posterior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, behind the posterior quadrangular lobule. Much of this lateral cerebrocerebellum is connected with the prefrontal and parietal cortex through the pons and dentate nucleus, and contributes to cognition as well as coordination of limb movements.

Inferior semilunar lobule.description: Crus II of the ansiform lobule (hemispheric lobule VIIA), below the horizontal fissure on the posterior-inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere. Part of the lateral cerebrocerebellum, involved in planning and coordinating skilled limb movements.

Gracile lobule.description: The paramedian lobule (hemispheric lobule VIIB) on the inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, between the inferior semilunar and biventral lobules. It receives spinal and cortical input and helps coordinate limb movements.

Biventral lobule.description: Hemispheric lobule VIII on the inferior surface of the cerebellum, lateral to the pyramis and in front of the tonsil, often split into two bellies. It contains a secondary somatotopic body map.

Wing of central lobule.description: Hemispheric continuation (lobules HII-HIII) of the central lobule of the vermis, in the anterior lobe of the cerebellum. It lies just behind the superior cerebellar peduncle and anterior medullary velum and is part of the spinocerebellum.

Peduncle of flocculus.description: Band of white matter joining the flocculus to the nodulus of the vermis, running along the free edge of the inferior medullary velum. Together they form the flocculonodular lobe (vestibulocerebellum), which controls balance, vestibulo-ocular reflexes and smooth pursuit; lesions cause nystagmus and truncal ataxia.

Intermediomedial nucleus.description: Column of neurons in the intermediate grey matter (lamina VII) of the spinal cord, medial to the intermediolateral column and near the central canal, present along the whole cord. It receives visceral afferent input from the dorsal roots and relays it to autonomic and sensory pathways.

Spinal reticular process.description: Reticulated zone of intermingled grey and white matter at the lateral base of the posterior horn, most distinct in the cervical spinal cord. It contains interneurons and propriospinal connections and is the spinal continuation of the brainstem reticular formation.

Superior gluteal nerve.description:
Branch of the sacral plexus (L4-S1) that leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen above piriformis with the superior gluteal vessels. It runs forward between gluteus medius and minimus and supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae.
Injury (for example from a misplaced intramuscular injection or hip surgery) weakens hip abduction: when standing on the affected leg the opposite side of the pelvis drops - a positive Trendelenburg sign.

Pudendal nerve.description:
The main nerve of the perineum, from the ventral rami of S2-S4. It leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, crosses behind the sacrospinous ligament near the ischial spine and re-enters through the lesser sciatic foramen into the pudendal (Alcock) canal on the lateral wall of the ischio-anal fossa.
Its branches - the inferior anal (rectal) nerves, the perineal nerve and the dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris - supply the external anal and urethral sphincters, the perineal muscles and the skin of the perineum and external genitalia. A pudendal block is given near the ischial spine; stretching during childbirth can cause faecal or urinary incontinence.

Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.description: Sensory branch of the sacral plexus (S1-S3) that leaves the pelvis below piriformis, runs down deep to gluteus maximus beside the sciatic nerve and then under the fascia lata along the back of the thigh. It supplies the skin of the lower buttock (inferior clunial nerves), the perineum and scrotum or labia (perineal branch), and the back of the thigh and popliteal fossa.

Anterior root of posterior femoral cutan.description: The contribution to the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve from the anterior divisions of the ventral rami of S2-S3. It joins the posterior root to form the nerve on the front of piriformis.

Posterior root of posterior femoral cuta.description: The contribution to the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve from the posterior divisions of the ventral rami of S1-S2. It joins the anterior root to form the nerve, which then leaves the pelvis below piriformis.

Inferior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv.description: Cutaneous branch of the radial nerve given off in the arm as it runs in the radial groove. It pierces the lateral head of triceps below the deltoid insertion and supplies the skin of the lower lateral arm (the upper lateral arm is supplied by the axillary nerve).

Superior subscapular nerve.description: Branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5-C6) that runs straight into the upper part of subscapularis, which it supplies.

Inferior subscapular nerve.description: Branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5-C6) that descends along the axillary border of the scapula and supplies the lower part of subscapularis and teres major.

Medial pectoral nerve.description: Branch of the medial cord of the brachial plexus (C8-T1). Despite its name it lies lateral to the lateral pectoral nerve on the chest wall. It passes between the axillary artery and vein, pierces pectoralis minor, which it supplies, and then enters the lower, sternocostal part of pectoralis major.

Infrapatellar branch of saphenous nerve.description: Branch of the saphenous nerve that pierces sartorius and the fascia lata and curves forward below the patella to supply the skin over the front of the knee and the patellar ligament. It is often cut during medial knee incisions and arthroscopy portals, leaving an area of numbness or a painful neuroma.

Medial crural cutaneous branches of saph.description: Cutaneous branches given off by the saphenous nerve as it descends with the great saphenous vein along the medial side of the leg. They supply the skin of the anteromedial and medial leg; they can be injured in varicose vein stripping or saphenous vein harvest.

Anterior cutaneous branches of femoral n.description: The intermediate and medial cutaneous nerves of the thigh: sensory branches of the femoral nerve that pierce the fascia lata to supply the skin of the front and medial side of the thigh down to the knee, where they join the patellar plexus.

Communicating branch of median nerve wit.description: Connection between the median and ulnar nerves. Such links are common and variable: in the palm between the common palmar digital nerves (Berrettini branch) or deep branches of the thenar muscles (Riche-Cannieu anastomosis), and in the forearm from the median to the ulnar nerve (Martin-Gruber anastomosis). They explain atypical patterns of weakness and sensory loss after nerve injury and confusing nerve conduction results in carpal or cubital tunnel syndrome.

Muscular branches of axillary nerve.description: Motor branches of the axillary nerve (C5-C6) after it passes through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery: the anterior branch winds around the surgical neck of the humerus to supply the deltoid, and the posterior branch supplies teres minor and the posterior deltoid. Fracture of the surgical neck or anterior shoulder dislocation may injure them, weakening abduction.

Muscular branches of median nerve.description: Motor branches of the median nerve: in the forearm to pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus and flexor digitorum superficialis, and via the anterior interosseous nerve to flexor pollicis longus, the lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus and pronator quadratus; in the hand the recurrent branch supplies abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis and the superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis, and digital branches supply the first two lumbricals.

Nerve to mylohyoid muscle.description: Branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve) given off just before it enters the mandibular foramen. It pierces the sphenomandibular ligament and runs in the mylohyoid groove on the inner surface of the mandible to supply mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric.

Nerve to piriformis muscle.description: Short branch from the sacral plexus (S1-S2) that enters the pelvic surface of piriformis directly.

Nerve to quadratus femoris muscle.description: Branch of the sacral plexus (L4-S1) that leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, deep (anterior) to the sciatic nerve. It descends on the back of the hip joint, which it supplies, and innervates quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus.
